summary: Read Neumann 1980 (Thm 2.1, verified in the PDF: for det odd there is a unique Wu set S, Σ_{i∈S}a_ij ≡ a_jj (2), and μ̄ = sign A(Γ) − Σ_{j∈S} e_j is an oriented-diffeo invariant, ≡ Rokhlin μ mod 16) and computed μ̄(L(n,A)) from the negative HJ chain for ALL 32 364 coprime pairs 0<A<n<400 (n odd) plus all 81 136 length-3 words at primes p≡1(4) <3·10⁴. Checks (0 failures): Wu set unique and never adjacent, μ̄(L(n,A*)) = μ̄(L(n,A)), μ̄(L(n,n−A)) = −μ̄; new exact identity μ̄(L(n,A)) = σ(K(n,A)) (Murasugi signature of the 2-bridge knot) on all 32 364 pairs (EVIDENCE; consistent with Lin–Ruberman–Saveliev d = −σ/4 as quoted in arXiv:2408.02857). Versus the ES sign: μ̄ mod 8 is exactly the Jacobi symbol (n≡1(8): (A/n)=−1 ⟺ μ̄≡4; n≡5(8): ⟺ μ̄≡0), and every one of the 81 136 words is a DK Thm 4.5 certificate iff μ̄ is in that class — i.e. bsA_wu_rokhlin_sign Theorem W in μ̄ form, nothing new; μ̄ mod 16 is a genuine refinement (two values per (n mod 16, J) cell, not fixed by the quartic symbol) but certificate status is already decided mod 8, so the integer/mod-16 part carries no ES information.
not_done: No proof of μ̄ = σ(K) (only checked n<400 and cited literature second-hand); mod-16 refinement not identified with a closed formula; no non-linear (star-shaped) plumbings.
next: None for ES; if wanted, identify μ̄ mod 16 of lens spaces via a Dedekind-sum formula (Kirby–Melvin).

summary: Per-class status: p≡3(4) and p≡5(8) are identity/boundary classes ((2/p)=−1 gives the length-2 non-residue A=2, λ(p)=2), only p≡1(8) needs DEDEKIND_ES Cor 4.6. For the 2-bridge knots K(p,A) (double cover L(p,A)) Arf=0 ⟺ p≡±1(8) for EVERY knot of determinant p (Levine; re-checked via Conway c₂ for all 32 364 pairs n<400), so Arf carries no per-prime information; with μ̄ = σ(K) (Z2800) σ≡0 (8) ⟺ (A/p)=+1 ⟺ the word is NOT a certificate (premise inverted: ES₅ needs a σ≡4 (8) knot). Over all 19 552 primes p≡1(8) <10⁶ every prime has a length-3 σ≡4 (8) knot (min 2 certificate words, p=17, 41); the σ≡0 (8) share is 0.299 overall, 0.417 at the 2 370 Mordell-hard primes vs 0.334 at residue-matched p≡1(24) controls, 0.362 at the 5 013 λ(p)=3 primes — the known residue-hardness effect (RESIDUE_HARDNESS.md), no knot-specific signal (EVIDENCE).
not_done: No Seifert-matrix construction (signature via Murasugi's formula / μ̄, Arf via Hartley Alexander polynomial instead); knots of det p that are not 2-bridge not considered.
next: None; the knot reading is the Jacobi sign again.

summary: Premise false as stated: for μ ≤ 3√p there are no ES (B = 1) points — for μ < √p Q_μ is definite (no river; 598 (p, μ) cases), and COMPOSITION_ES Thm 1.3 forbids B = 1 for μ ≤ n; the 1 235 rivers with √p < μ ≤ 3√p (p ≡ 1 (4) < 500) carry 250 V_n points (B > 1) and 0 ES points. Doing the step on the correct range (all μ ≤ p² + p + (p+1)/4), a run-compressed topograph walk of Q_μ = pA² − 2μAB + B² finds all 268 ES points (matches a brute-force C count, 268) on the river, every one at the same place: walking from the principal face (0,1) (value 1) across the edge to (1, μ), the river runs are (−, μ−1), (+, 1), (−, 2j−1), and the ES face (2j, 1) of value −(4tj−1) is the last face of the third run (268/268; 71 of them have D > √(μ²−p), i.e. outside Lagrange's zone, still on the river). So the topograph shows exactly MARKOFF_ES Thm 4.3 / COMPOSITION_ES Thm 1.3: one fixed slot near the principal value whose value must divide μ — no pattern along the period beyond that, and the period (12–110 runs in the examples) plays no role.
not_done: No drawings; no statistics of V_n points with B > 1 along full periods beyond the μ ≤ 3√p count; p restricted to < 500 as the item specified.
next: None; the river reading is the depth-3 CF dictionary already in MARKOFF_ES §4.

summary: Implemented the lattice-level braid action on semiorthogonal Gram matrices G = [[d1,a,b],[0,d2,c],[0,0,d3]] (Bondal mutation e_{i+1} − (χ(e_i,e_{i+1})/d_i)e_i, rational for d_i ≠ 1) and checked symbolically (sympy): semiorthogonality is kept, the diagonal is permuted, the braid relation holds, and det(Gᵀ + sG) is invariant, with s²-coefficient 3d1d2d3 − (d3a² + d2b² + d1c² − abc) (PROVED, symbolic). The item's d = (1,n,1) gives the invariant a² + nb² + c² − abc, a weighted Markoff surface with all three variables squared, NOT S_{n,D}: nA² + B² + D = ABC; the latter appears iff one weight is 0 (degenerate Gram, det 0), e.g. d = (0,1,n), (a,b,c) = (A,B,C), where the invariant equals exactly D (all 24 diagonal/dictionary matches have a zero weight). A zero-weight object cannot be mutated across (division by 0), so σ1^{±2} is undefined and σ2² needs n | C; a BFS over all integral left/right mutations from 5 S_{n,D} points (n = 5, 13, 17, 29, 41) gives orbits of 3 states with 1 point in the original frame, against the infinite Vieta/Pell orbit of MARKOFF_ES Prop 2.1 / GROWING_MUTE Prop 1.2 — no new infinite group action from this categorical source.
not_done: Did not read Bondal–Polishchuk itself (mutation formula used is the standard Bondal one, from memory); no search for an actual triangulated category realising d = (0,1,n) (e.g. with a spherical/zero-Euler object); sign/shift changes not added to the BFS (they do not change divisibility).
next: None for ES; the d = (1,n,1) weighted Markoff surface is a different equation.

summary: Read Cohn–Kumar (arXiv:1307.0443, Thm 1.1: metacommutation by a Hurwitz prime Q of norm q ≠ p permutes the p+1 primes of norm p mod left units with sign (q/p), identity if Q ≡ integer mod p, else 1 + ((Re Q)² − q / p) fixed points) and implemented Hurwitz arithmetic (Euclidean right-gcd, metacommutation PQ = Q′P′); the theorem re-checks with 0 failures on all 2 740 (p, q, Q), p, q < 42. ES side: for all 170 Type I tuples (a,b,c,d,e) of p ≡ 1 (4) < 200 (repo enumeration as quat_typeI.py), 8 have d ≡ 7 (8)-type (no pure Hurwitz w of norm d: ℚ(√−d) does not embed in B_{2,∞}); for the other 162, with w² = −d, α = 1+2aw, β = 1+2bw, γ = 2cw − p (αβ = eγ), the factorisation α = F·E, β = E^σ·G (E of norm e) holds in all 162 cases, and metacommutation on the norm-p primes is: by w a fixed-point-free involution (sign −1, cycle type 2^{(p+1)/2}, 162/162), by γ sign −1 / 0 fixed points (162/162), by α, β signs (Nα/p) = −(Nβ/p) (96 / 66 split), 0 fixed points. All of this is PROVED from CK: for X = r + s·w, (Re X)² − N X = −s²d, so fixed points = 1 + (−d/p) = 0 is QUATERNION_ES Prop 1.3's genus condition, and the signs are Legendre symbols of norms — the metacommutation 'ES sign' is the genus character again (B1), with no further invariant.
not_done: Type II data not placed in the Hurwitz order (it lives in (−d,−p), not B_{2,∞}); no Lipschitz-only variant; cycle structures beyond fixed points / involution type not compared with Leite 2025 (arXiv:2504.08709).
next: None; every metacommutation invariant here is a Legendre symbol of a norm.

summary: Implemented Brandt matrices from scratch (Pizer maximal orders of B_{p,∞}, left-ideal classes by 2-neighbour BFS closed by Eichler's mass Σ1/|O_i^×| = (p−1)/24, exact lattice products + LLL/Fincke–Pohst counts, Gross's convention B_ij(m) = #{b ∈ I_j⁻¹I_i : nrd b·N(I_j)/N(I_i) = m}/|O_j^×|) for all 44 primes 5 ≤ p < 200 and m ≤ 20 (h up to 17): B(1) = I, row sums σ(m), B(m)B(n) = B(mn) hold everywhere, and the Eichler–Gross trace formula tr B(m) = Σ_{s²≤4m} H_p(4m − s²) matches all 870 (p, m) exactly (PROVED-by-check of the implementation). ES side: by that formula tr B_p(m) is an affine function of the Legendre symbols (d/p) for the 39 discriminants |d| ≤ 4m (numerical residual 2·10⁻⁹); across 4 174 primes p ≡ 1 (4) in [10⁴, 10⁵] the level counts R_C(p) = #{d | 4Cp+1 : d ≡ −1 (4C)} (C ≤ 8, FRONTIER §2.1) correlate with traces up to |r| = 0.46 (R_1 vs tr B(13); permutation null 95 % = 0.056), but only through those characters (e.g. 3 | 4p+1 ⟺ (−3/p) = −1): R² of ΣR_C on 30 traces 0.277 vs 0.279 on the 39 symbols and 0.263 on 10 small symbols. No exact identity: R_C(p) never equals tr B_p(4C) (0/105), and 'R_C(p) is an entry of B_p(C) or B_p(4C)' hits 192/271 vs 194/271 for a random other prime (EVIDENCE) — Brandt data sees ES level counts only via the residue class of p, as z9_brandt_screen L1/L2 predicted.
not_done: Gross 1987 not re-read (trace-formula normalisation fixed by the exact match instead); no Brandt matrices for Eichler orders of level 4C (non-prime 'ES levels'); ternary Gross-lattice theta series (the objects in DISCOVERIES Cor 2.2) not computed; entries only for m ≤ 20.
next: None; a Brandt route would have to act on ray-class data of individual classes (z9 L3), not on traces.
